# moorage 0.0.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/moorage/0.0.1

# moorage

Install your self-authored agent **skills and plugins** into one central home, and
wire every agent harness to them from a single source of truth. A small Rust CLI.

*(Renamed from  skilldock, which collided on GitHub.)*

## Commands

```
moorage install   SOURCE [--mode dev|normal] [--skills a,b] [--harnesses claude,pi,omp,codex]
                         [--force] [--dry-run] [--no-post-install]
moorage uninstall NAME... [--dry-run]
moorage update    NAME... [--force] [--dry-run]
moorage list
moorage doctor    [--json]
```
All commands accept the six root overrides (see *Roots* below). `--dry-run` prints the
full action plan — skills, links, hook placements, registration merges, backups,
post_install — and mutates nothing.

## Skills (no manifest — behavior unchanged)

`SOURCE` may be a directory containing `SKILL.md` (single skill) or a repo with
`skills/*/SKILL.md` (multi-skill; scanned one level). The skill **name** comes from
the `SKILL.md` frontmatter `name:` and must be lowercase `[a-z0-9-]`, ≤ 64 chars,
with a non-empty `description:` (pi's discovery rule — enforced so the link name is
correct). A `skills/*` layout is **preferred** over a repo-root `SKILL.md`, so a repo
carrying both installs its `skills/<name>` payloads (the baseline shape).

Each skill installs to `~/.moorage/skills/{name}`:

| Mode | `~/.moorage/skills/{name}`is | Use it when |
|---|---|---|
| `dev`(default) | a symlink to the repo payload | authoring / iterating |
| `normal`(alias:`local`) | a real copy (excludes `.git`,`__pycache__`) | pinned snapshot |

and the agent roots link into the home:

```
~/.agents/skills/{name}  --+                              +-- dev:    repo payload (live)
                           +-->  ~/.moorage/skills/{name} -+
~/.claude/skills/{name}  --+                              +-- normal: a copy in the home
```
oh-my-pi reads both locations; all agents dedupe by real path.

## Plugins (`moorage.toml` manifest)

A `moorage.toml` at the repo root (or passed directly as `SOURCE`) upgrades a repo to
a plugin. **Its absence changes nothing** — no-manifest repos keep the exact behavior
above.

```
 = "conversate"          # optional plugin label (names placed hook files)
[]                    # optional preferences (see Precedence)
 = "dev"                 # dev | normal | local
 = ["claude", "pi", "omp", "codex"]
[[]]
 = "."                   # payload dir, repo-root-relative ("." = repo root)
 = "normal"              # optional per-skill override
 = ["claude"]       # optional per-skill override
[[]]
 = "hooks/claude/settings-snippet.json"   # merged into <claude-root>/settings.json
[[]]
 = "hooks/pi/conv-turn-counter.ts"         # placed into <pi-root>/agent/extensions/
[[]]
 = "hooks/pi/conv-turn-counter.ts"         # placed into <omp-root>/hooks/{stage}/
 = "pre"                                    # default "pre" when omitted
[[]]
 = "hooks/codex/hooks.json"                # merged into <codex-root>/hooks.json
[]
 = ["python scripts/example.py init"]         # optional; cwd = canonical skill dir
```
### Preference precedence

`CLI flags > per-skill entry > [install] table > built-in defaults` (mode `dev`, all
four harnesses). `--mode` / `--harnesses` on the command line mean "override the
manifest". The `harnesses` list gates both the skill links (`claude` → claude-root
link; any of `pi`/`omp`/`codex` → agents-root link) and the hook wiring per harness.
Per-skill `harnesses` gate that skill's links; plugin-level hooks follow
`CLI > [install] > default`.

### Hook FILES (pi, omp)

Placed as **file symlinks** named `moorage-{label}-{basename}` (label = manifest
`name`, else the first skill's name) pointing at the canonical copy inside
`~/.moorage/skills/{name}/...` — so dev/normal switching is transparent. If file
symlinks are unavailable (Windows without Developer Mode) the file is **copied** with
a loud warning, and doctor tracks drift of copied placements. Junctions are dir-only
and hardlinks die across volumes, so neither is used for files. Hook scripts must
live inside a `[[skills]]` payload (otherwise no canonical home copy exists — the
install refuses that hook).

### Registration MERGES (claude, codex)

The snippet's `hooks` block merges into the target config via a serde_json
round-trip that preserves unrelated keys:

- claude → `<claude-root>/settings.json`
- codex → `<codex-root>/hooks.json`(plus a printed reminder that codex loads hooks only with`[features] hooks = true`in`~/.codex/config.toml`— moorage**never**edits that file)

Merges are **append-if-absent** (exact-equality dedupe ⇒ idempotent re-installs), and
a syntactically invalid target config is refused, never clobbered. Before the
**first** modification of each config, a `.bak` copy goes into `~/.moorage/backups/`
(named `{basename}.{epoch}.bak`, recorded in state).

**Command-path rewriting** (design ruling; the v2 exact rule is unrecovered): every
whitespace-separated token of a `command` / `commandWindows` string that resolves —
relative to an installed skill payload root — to an existing file is rewritten to the
absolute path of that file under the canonical home
(`~/.moorage/skills/{name}/...`). The **home** path, never the source repo path, so
dev-mode symlinks keep the loop live. Rewritten paths containing spaces are quoted; a
token that itself contains spaces can never match (whitespace split — a known v2
limitation). Snippets should therefore reference their scripts by payload-relative
paths (e.g. `hooks/claude/counter.ps1`).

### Reversibility

Every inserted JSON entry is persisted **verbatim** in `state.toml` *and* is
self-marked by containing the `~/.moorage/skills/{name}` path in its command (no
marker keys are injected — that would fight harness schema validation). `uninstall`:

- unmerges exactly the recorded entries (falling back to the home-path marker for
entries a user edited in place); emptied configs are left as `{}`, never deleted;
- removes placed hook files and agent links (links are dropped, targets untouched);
- removes the home entry — for dev mode the **symlink only**, never the target repo;
- deletes the state record.

Source repositories are never touched. Legacy state records (pre-plugin, five fields)
still load; uninstalling one derives the two conventional agent-link paths and
deletes each **only after verifying it actually points into the moorage home** —
anything else is skipped with a warning.

### post_install

Commands run after all components are placed, with `cwd` = the canonical skill dir in
the home (first skill for multi-skill plugins). Each command is echoed and its
outcome recorded in state. `--no-post-install` skips them (recorded as `skipped`). A
failing command **reports loudly, marks the state record ( failed(N)), sets exit
code 1, and does NOT roll back the install** (design ruling — fix the cause and
re-run, or uninstall).

`update` never runs post_install.## update

- **dev**installs: verify and repair the whole chain — home link, agent links, hook files; re-apply merges when snippets changed (stale recorded entries are unmerged, new ones merged; stale hook files removed).
- **normal**installs: hash-compare (in-crate FNV-1a-64 over the payload tree) and re-copy- **only if the source changed**;- **refuse**when the installed copy was hand-edited (or when a legacy record has no stored hash to verify against) —- `--force`overrides.

## doctor

Read-only, always. Checks: state.toml parse health; full chain integrity (agent link
→ home → payload); dangling/re-targeted links; placed hook files (missing, dangling,
copy drift vs canonical); merged registrations (recorded entries still present,
target configs valid); **orphaned** moorage-marked entries (home path in the command
but absent from state); unmanaged entries (reported, never touched) incl. pi
name-rule violations; shadowing (same name under claude-root and agents-root
resolving to different real paths); normal-mode content drift vs source; dev-mode git
hygiene (dirty tree, non-main branch — best effort); manifest preference drift
(manifest prefers a different mode than installed); `AGENTS.md` inside a skill dir
(pi issue #2473). `--json` emits the findings machine-readably. Exit code is 0 even
with findings; nonzero means doctor itself failed to run.

## Conflicts, idempotency, dry-run

- An entry already resolving to the right target is left alone (idempotent re-runs); merges dedupe by exact equality.
- A conflicting foreign entry is **refused**with a clear message;`--force`renames it to a sibling`{name}.bak-N`and replaces it.
- `--dry-run`prints the full plan and changes nothing (configs are only read).

## Roots (for tests / alternate setups)

Flag > env > default, uniformly:

| Setting | Flag | Env | Default | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| home | `--home` | `MOORAGE_HOME` | `~/.moorage` | canonical home, state, backups |
| agents root | `--agents-root` | `MOORAGE_AGENTS_ROOT` | `~/.agents` | pi/omp/codex skill links |
| claude root | `--claude-root` | `MOORAGE_CLAUDE_ROOT` | `~/.claude` | Claude skill links + `settings.json`merges |
| pi root | `--pi-root` | `MOORAGE_PI_ROOT` | `~/.pi` | hook files under `agent/extensions/` |
| omp root | `--omp-root` | `MOORAGE_OMP_ROOT` | `~/.omp` | hook files under `hooks/{stage}/` |
| codex root | `--codex-root` | `MOORAGE_CODEX_ROOT` | `~/.codex` | `hooks.json`merges |

## state.toml

`~/.moorage/state.toml` records, per skill: `name`, `mode`, `source`, `installed`/
`updated` (epoch secs), and — for plugin installs — `plugin` label, `manifest` path,
effective `harnesses`, `home_kind` (symlink/junction/copy), `copy_hash` (normal
mode), `[[links]]` (path/kind/target), `[[hook_files]]` (path/kind/target),
`[[merges]]` (file/event/verbatim entry), `[[post_install]]` (command/status), and
`[[backups]]` (original/backup). Legacy five-field records load unchanged.

## Windows link fallback

Directory links try: real symlink (needs Developer Mode or elevation) → NTFS
**junction** via `cmd /c mklink /J` (no privileges) → **copy** with a loud warning.
File placements try: file symlink → copy (drift tracked by doctor). On non-Windows,
symlinks are used directly.

## Unverified upstream paths (honesty notes)

- **omp**: upstream documents only- *project-level*- `.omp/hooks/{stage}/*.ts`discovery. The user-level- `<omp-root>/hooks/{stage}/`placement is a- **best-documented-guess**(unverified upstream). doctor emits a- `warn`note when omp hook files are installed; override with- `--omp-root`.
- **codex**: whether codex reads a- *user-level*- `hooks.json`at all is- **unverified**(only project-level- `.codex/hooks.json`is documented). doctor emits a- `warn`note when codex merges are installed; override with- `--codex-root`.
- **pi**(- `~/.pi/agent/extensions`) and- **claude**(- `~/.claude/settings.json`) are documented/known paths.

## Design rulings (unrecovered v2 details, decided here)

- **Command rewriting token rule**: whitespace token → resolve against installed payload roots (manifest order, first match) → rewrite to the absolute canonical home path; quote only when the result contains spaces; absolute tokens skipped.
- **Mode name**: the CLI keeps- `dev|normal`;- `local`(the v2 name) is accepted as an alias both on the CLI and in manifests.
- **omp**:- `stage`default- `"pre"`(the only value ever observed).
- **post_install failure**: loud warning +- `failed(N)`in state + exit 1, no rollback;- `--no-post-install`records- `skipped`;- `update`never runs post_install.
- `--force`backups- `{name}.bak-N`convention (the pinned minimal-Rust behavior) instead of moving into- `~/.moorage/backups/`; the backups dir holds config- `.bak`snapshots only, named- `{basename}.{epoch}.bak`.
- **backups/ contents are permanent**: uninstall does not delete taken backups (traceability).
- **Multi-skill plugins**: post_install cwd = first skill's canonical dir; hook artifacts are named after the manifest- `name`(else the first skill); the plugin component ledger (hook files, merges, post_install, backups) rides on the first skill's state record.
- **Manifests must declare**: a manifest with no skills entry is an error (hooks need a payload to live in).- `[[skills]]`
- **Corrupt state.toml**: mutating commands refuse to run over an unparseable ledger (protecting the live records); doctor reports it as a- `fail`finding.
- `update`flags- `--force`(attested) plus- `--dry-run`(inferred-carried).
- **Content hashing**: in-crate FNV-1a-64 (stable across releases, zero deps) — std's- `DefaultHasher`is explicitly not used for persisted hashes.

## Build

```
cargo build --release          # binary at target/release/moorage(.exe)
cargo install --path .         # optional: install to ~/.cargo/bin
```
Tests: `cargo test` (unit: manifest parse, merge/unmerge/rewrite, state round-trip
incl. legacy records) and `python -m pytest tests/ -q` (29 black-box tests against
the built binary with all six roots pinned to temp dirs; set `MOORAGE_BIN` to point
at a specific exe, else `target/debug/moorage`).

Requires a stable Rust toolchain. Dependencies: `clap` (CLI), `serde` + `toml`
(manifests + state), `serde_json` (registration merges).

# polkadot_jemalloc_shim - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/polkadot-jemalloc-shim/0.6.0/polkadot_jemalloc_shim/

## Expand description

Shim crate to enable `jemalloc-allocator` feature for Polkadot crates.

Because [there doesn’t exist any easier way right now](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/1197), we
need an entire crate to handle `jemalloc` enabling/disabling. This way we can enable it by
default on Linux, but have it optional on all other OSes.

# sim_lib_sound_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-sound-core/0.1.0-rc.1/sim_lib_sound_core/

## Expand description

Core sound primitives for the SIM music constellation.

This crate defines the foundational acoustic types shared by the
sound/synthesis layer: [ Frequency](https://docs.rs/struct.Frequency.html),

[, and](https://docs.rs/struct.Amplitude.html)

`Amplitude`[quantities; the](https://docs.rs/struct.Phase.html)

`Phase`[,](https://docs.rs/struct.Partial.html)

`Partial`[, and](https://docs.rs/struct.Envelope.html)

`Envelope`[models that build a spectral tone from sinusoidal components; and helpers for default envelopes and equal-temperament pitch-to-frequency conversion.](https://docs.rs/struct.Tone.html)

`Tone`## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Amplitude](https://docs.rs/struct.Amplitude.html)
- A non-negative linear amplitude.
- [Envelope](https://docs.rs/struct.Envelope.html)
- An attack/decay/sustain/release amplitude envelope.
- [Frequency](https://docs.rs/struct.Frequency.html)
- A positive frequency in hertz.
- [Partial](https://docs.rs/struct.Partial.html)
- A single sinusoidal component of a tone.
- [Phase](https://docs.rs/struct.Phase.html)
- A phase angle in radians.
- [Tone](https://docs.rs/struct.Tone.html)
- A complete tone: a set of `Partial``Envelope`

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Envelope](https://docs.rs/enum.EnvelopeShape.html)- Shape
- The interpolation curve applied across an `Envelope`
- [Sound](https://docs.rs/enum.SoundCoreError.html)- Core - Error
- Error raised when sound primitives are constructed with invalid values.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [default_](https://docs.rs/fn.default_envelope.html)- envelope
- Returns a general-purpose default envelope (short attack and decay, high sustain, moderate release, linear shape).
- [equal_](https://docs.rs/fn.equal_temperament_frequency.html)- temperament_ - frequency
- Returns the 12-tone equal-temperament frequency of `pitch`, with A4 (MIDI 69) anchored at 440 Hz.

# vize_fresco - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/vize_fresco/0.273.0/vize_fresco/

## Expand description

Fresco - Vue TUI Framework

A high-performance Terminal User Interface framework for Vue.js, similar to React Ink but built with Rust for performance.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- **Terminal Control**: Cross-platform terminal handling via crossterm
- **Flexbox Layout**: Layout engine powered by taffy
- **CJK Support**: Full Unicode text handling including Japanese IME
- **Efficient Rendering**: Double-buffered differential rendering

[§](https://docs.rs#architecture)Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Vue Components                        │
│                  (Box, Text, Input)                       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                          │
                          ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                  Vue Custom Renderer                     │
│                    (TypeScript)                          │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                          │
                          ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   NAPI Bindings                          │
│             (Rust <-> Node.js bridge)                    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                          │
        ┌─────────────────┼─────────────────┐
        ▼                 ▼                 ▼
┌───────────────┐ ┌───────────────┐ ┌───────────────┐
│   Terminal    │ │    Layout     │ │    Render     │
│   (backend,   │ │   (taffy,     │ │   (tree,      │
│    buffer)    │ │    flex)      │ │    diff)      │
└───────────────┘ └───────────────┘ └───────────────┘
        │                                   │
        ▼                                   ▼
┌───────────────┐                 ┌───────────────┐
│     Input     │                 │     Text      │
│  (keyboard,   │                 │   (width,     │
│   mouse, ime) │                 │    segment)   │
└───────────────┘                 └───────────────┘
```

# vize_musea - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/vize_musea/0.273.0/vize_musea/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#vize_musea)vize_musea

Musea - Component gallery and documentation for Vize.

[§](https://docs.rs#name-origin)Name Origin

**Musea** (plural of museum) represents a gallery space where art is
displayed and documented. Similarly, `vize_musea` provides a gallery
for Vue components, allowing developers to view and interact with
components in isolation - similar to Storybook.

[§](https://docs.rs#concepts)Concepts

- **Art**: A component variation/state (replaces “story”)
- **Art file**(- `*.art.vue`): File defining arts
- **Gallery**: Display area for arts
- **Palette**: Interactive controls panel

[§](https://docs.rs#performance)Performance

This crate is optimized for high performance:

- **Zero-copy parsing**: All strings are borrowed from source
- **Arena allocation**: Uses- `vize_carton::Bump`for fast allocation
- **Minimal allocations**: Only allocates when absolutely necessary
- **Fast byte-level parsing**: Uses- `memchr`and- `memmem`for O(n) search

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

```
use vize_carton::Bump;
use vize_musea::{parse_art, transform_to_csf};
use vize_musea::types::ArtParseOptions;
let allocator = Bump::new();
let source = r#"
<script setup lang="ts">
defineArt("./Button.vue", { title: "Button" });
</script>
<art>
  <variant name="Primary" default>
    <Button variant="primary">Click me</Button>
  </variant>
  <variant name="Secondary">
    <Button variant="secondary">Click me</Button>
  </variant>
</art>
"#;
// Parse Art file with arena allocator
let art = parse_art(&allocator, source, ArtParseOptions::default()).unwrap();
// Transform to Storybook CSF
let csf = transform_to_csf(&art);
println!("Generated: {}", csf.filename);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- Zero-copy parsing of `*.art.vue`files
- Type-safe variant definitions
- Storybook CSF 3.0 export
- Visual Regression Testing (VRT) support
- Interactive props palette

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use parse::`- [parse_art](https://docs.rs/parse/fn.parse_art.html);
- `pub use tokens::`- [build_token_map](https://docs.rs/tokens/fn.build_token_map.html);

# vize_atelier_sfc - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/vize_atelier_sfc/0.273.0/vize_atelier_sfc/

## Expand description

Vue Single File Component (.vue) compiler.

This module provides parsing and compilation of Vue SFCs, following the Vue.js core structure:

- `parse`- SFC parsing into descriptor blocks
- `compile_script`- Script/script setup compilation
- `compile_template`- Template block compilation (DOM and Vapor)
- `compile`- Main SFC compilation orchestration
- `style`- Style block compilation with scoped CSS
- `css`- Low-level CSS compilation with LightningCSS

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use vize_atelier_sfc::{parse_sfc, compile_sfc, SfcParseOptions, SfcCompileOptions};
let source = r#"
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
const count = ref(0)
</script>
<template>
  <button @click="count++">{{ count }}</button>
</template>
"#;
let descriptor = parse_sfc(source, SfcParseOptions::default()).unwrap();
let result = compile_sfc(&descriptor, SfcCompileOptions::default()).unwrap();
println!("{}", result.code);
```
